sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是百分之九十九隐形。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: Around the corner from our office in beautiful downtown Oakland, California, is DeLauer's newsstand.
sentences.zh: 在美丽的加利福尼亚州奥克兰市中心，我们办公室的拐角处，有一家德劳尔报摊。

sentences.en: It has been there since 1907.
sentences.zh: 它自1907年起就一直开在那里。

sentences.en: For the people who live and work downtown, it is central to our existence.
sentences.zh: 对于在市中心生活和工作的人们来说，它是我们生活的中枢。

sentences.en: Everyone goes there to buy drinks, lottery tickets, little packs of fruit-flavored cigarillos,
sentences.zh: 每个人都去那里买饮料、彩票、一小包果味小雪茄，

sentences.en: and occasionally, even a newspaper.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，甚至还会买份报纸。

sentences.en: But about eight months ago, it became clear that even though DeLauer's wants a bunch of people inside the store buying things,
sentences.zh: 但在大约八个月前，情况变得明朗起来：尽管德劳尔报摊希望店里有一堆人进来买东西，

sentences.en: they don't want a bunch of people outside their store hanging out on the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 但他们不希望一群人在店外的人行道上闲晃。

sentences.en: Here's how you can tell.
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看出来的呢？

sentences.en: DeLauer's started playing really loud classical music through a speaker outside.
sentences.zh: 德劳尔报摊开始通过外面的扬声器播放很大声的古典音乐。

sentences.en: And although I still see a fair number of people hanging out in front of the place,
sentences.zh: 虽然我还是能看到相当多的人在店门前闲逛，

sentences.en: the owner says it's not nearly as many as before.
sentences.zh: 但店主说，人数已经远不如前了。

sentences.en: Oh, big change.
sentences.zh: 哦，巨大的改变。

sentences.en: It was mess.
sentences.zh: 那是一团糟。

sentences.en: They hung out outside and, you know, just they're playing dice on the street outside the door.
sentences.zh: 他们在外面闲逛，你知道的，就在门外的街上玩骰子。

sentences.en: And it was crazy.
sentences.zh: 这太疯狂了。

sentences.en: But now it helps us a lot.
sentences.zh: 但现在它帮了我们大忙。

sentences.en: Even the customer telling us they see the change on the street here.
sentences.zh: 甚至连顾客都告诉我们，他们看到了这里街道上的变化。

sentences.en: I'm the owner of DeLauer's newsstand.
sentences.zh: 我是德劳尔报摊的店主。

sentences.en: My name is Fasil Lema.
sentences.zh: 我叫法西尔·莱马。

sentences.en: When you have classical music, people who are young and cool don't really hang out there.
sentences.zh: 当你放古典音乐时，年轻且酷的人就不会真的在那里闲逛了。

sentences.en: So that's a way to deter teenagers.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种阻吓青少年的方法。

sentences.en: That is Selena Savic.
sentences.zh: 那是塞莱娜·萨维奇。

sentences.en: And I am co-author of the research project about unpleasant design.
sentences.zh: 我是关于不愉快设计研究项目的共同作者。

sentences.en: Playing classical music on loudspeakers is an example of what Selena calls unpleasant design.
sentences.zh: 在扬声器上播放古典音乐，就是塞莱娜所称的不愉快设计的一个例子。

sentences.en: Unpleasant design is something that works well at deterring certain behaviors and certain uses from particularly public spaces.
sentences.zh: 不愉快设计是指在阻止特定行为和特定用途方面非常有效的设计，尤其针对公共空间。

sentences.en: Along with her partner, Gordon Savic, Selena collects and catalogs unpleasant designs.
sentences.zh: 塞莱娜和她的伴侣戈登·萨维奇一起收集并分类了各种不愉快设计。

sentences.en: Unpleasant design was here since we started designing public space or since we started designing cities.
sentences.zh: 自从我们开始设计公共空间或城市以来，不愉快设计就一直存在。

sentences.en: Unpleasant designs are meant to exert a kind of social control in public by targeting people who spend a lot of time in public spaces,
sentences.zh: 不愉快设计旨在通过针对那些在公共空间花费大量时间的人群，在公共场所施加一种社会控制，

sentences.en: especially the young and the homeless.
sentences.zh: 特别是年轻人和无家可归者。

sentences.en: And the designs often end up pushing these so-called undesirable people out of one space and into another.
sentences.zh: 这些设计往往最终会将这些所谓的“不受欢迎的人”从一个空间驱赶到另一个空间。

sentences.en: Music is only one method for deterring teens from public space.
sentences.zh: 音乐只是阻止青少年进入公共空间的方法之一。

sentences.en: In 2009, the Nottinghamshire Housing Estates in England installed pink lighting to keep kids from congregating.
sentences.zh: 2009年，英格兰的诺丁汉郡住房庄园安装了粉色灯光，以阻止孩子们聚集。

sentences.en: Pink lights, which would emphasize the skin, like, blemishes on teenagers, which should result in teenagers not hanging out there.
sentences.zh: 粉色灯光会强调皮肤上的瑕疵，比如青少年的瑕疵，从而导致青少年不再在那里闲逛。

sentences.en: That's one of my favorite examples.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的例子之一。

sentences.en: Mine too, although there's not a lot of evidence that proves how effective it is.
sentences.zh: 我也是，尽管没有太多证据证明它有多大效果。

sentences.en: Pink lighting that preys on teenagers' insecurities is funny and kind of devious, if a little far-fetched.
sentences.zh: 利用青少年不安全感的粉色灯光既滑稽又有些狡猾，虽然有点牵强。

sentences.en: Another more substantiated example of targeting and trying to eliminate undesirable behavior with light is the presence of blue lighting in public restrooMs.
sentences.zh: 另一个更有据可查的利用光线来针对并试图消除不良行为的例子，是公共卫生间内蓝色灯光的存在。

sentences.en: I saw this in UK train stations quite a bit last time I was there.
sentences.zh: 我上次去英国火车站时经常看到这个。

sentences.en: Blue light of a particular color makes the veins slightly less visible.
sentences.zh: 特定颜色的蓝光会使静脉不那么明显。

sentences.en: You can't see your veins through your skin, so it's hard to find a target if you're an intravenous drug user.
sentences.zh: 你无法透过皮肤看到自己的静脉，所以如果你是静脉吸毒者，就很难找到注射目标。

sentences.en: Then it became a very popular solution for all kind of publicly accessible toilets and even sometimes in buses.
sentences.zh: 后来它成了一种非常受欢迎的解决方案，适用于各种公共厕所，有时甚至在公交车上也有。

sentences.en: When your veins are not visible to you, you're obviously not going to be able to take any heroin.
sentences.zh: 当你看不到自己的静脉时，你显然就无法注射海洛因了。

sentences.en: According to Selena, lights are one of the original forms of public social control.
sentences.zh: 据塞莱娜说，灯光是最初的公共社会控制形式之一。

sentences.en: For example.
sentences.zh: 举个例子。

sentences.en: There was a bridge in a small town in Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 波斯尼亚一个小镇上曾有一座桥。

sentences.en: Specifically in the Kasbah of Visegrad, Bosnia in the early 1900s.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，是20世纪初波斯尼亚维谢格拉德的卡斯巴。

sentences.en: Where the Austrian government, who kind of annexed the country at that time, decided to implement street lighting.
sentences.zh: 当时吞并了该国的奥地利政府决定安装路灯。

sentences.en: And that was very unpleasant to the locals.
sentences.zh: 这对当地人来说非常不愉快。

sentences.en: And the locals would destroy the light every night and the government would reinstall it every morning.
sentences.zh: 当地人每天晚上都会毁坏路灯，而政府每天早上又会重新安装。

sentences.en: And so the idea that light is something unpleasant for free expression in public space is something that we completely forgot.
sentences.zh: 因此，光线会妨碍公共空间自由表达这一令人不快的观念，已经被我们完全遗忘了。

sentences.en: We've since become so habituated to public lighting that our primary experience with streetlights is that they deter criminal activity and make us feel safe.
sentences.zh: 我们后来对公共照明习以为常，以至于我们对路灯的主要体验是它们能震慑犯罪活动并让我们感到安全。

sentences.en: Unless you're someone who laments the lack of stars in the night sky or lives in an apartment with a window right next to a screamingly bright bulb,
sentences.zh: 除非你是那种感叹夜空中缺乏星星的人，或者住在窗户紧挨着刺眼亮灯的公寓里，

sentences.en: you might never view streetlights as unpleasant at all.
sentences.zh: 否则你可能永远不会觉得路灯是不愉快的。

sentences.en: Which is one of the reasons why the Unpleasant Design Project wants to point it out,
sentences.zh: 这也是不愉快设计项目想要指出这一点的原因之一，

sentences.en: so that it gets recognized as being part of an overall design scheme that can take on a much uglier manifestation.
sentences.zh: 以便人们认识到它是整体设计方案的一部分，而这种方案可能会呈现出更加丑陋的面貌。

sentences.en: Well, these studs may only be a few centimeters tall, but they've caused a big debate.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些突起可能只有几厘米高，但它们引发了巨大的争论。

sentences.en: This is from a BBC News story from 2014.
sentences.zh: 这是来自2014年BBC新闻的一则报道。

sentences.en: The reporter Nick Beak is pointing to a set of angry-looking spikes that were installed in the concrete floor of a small alcove by the entrance to an apartment building.
sentences.zh: 记者尼克·比克正指着一套看起来气势汹汹的尖刺，它们被安装在公寓楼入口处一个小凹室的混凝土底座上。

sentences.en: The spikes are clearly meant to stop people from sitting or lying there.
sentences.zh: 这些尖刺显然是为了阻止人们在那里坐着或躺着。

sentences.en: Is this a legitimate way to prevent rough sleeping and possible antisocial behavior?
sentences.zh: 这是防止露宿街头和可能的反社会行为的合情合理的方法吗？

sentences.en: Or are they a symbol of a heartless approach to homelessness?
sentences.zh: 还是说它们是无情对待无家可归者的象征？

sentences.en: Hey, do you want to know the answer?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你想知道答案吗？

sentences.en: It's the second one.
sentences.zh: 是后者。

sentences.en: That spiked a huge debate, and even the mayor of London reacted and said that they should be removed
sentences.zh: 这引发了巨大的争论，甚至伦敦市长也做出反应并表示应该将它们移除，

sentences.en: and that we should not address homeless people in this way.
sentences.zh: 并且我们不应该以这种方式对待无家可归的人。

sentences.en: The grocery chain Tesco also added spikes to areas outside the entrance to one of its stores in central London in 2014.
sentences.zh: 2014年，连锁超市乐购也在伦敦市中心其一家分店入口外的区域添加了尖刺。

sentences.en: They were removed after days of public proteSt.
sentences.zh: 在公众抗议几天后，它们被移除了。

sentences.en: Generally, the debate was about the way we treat homelessness,
sentences.zh: 总的来说，这场争论是关于我们对待无家可归者的方式，

sentences.en: and is that something that we just want to remove from a particular space,
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是我们要从特定空间中清除的东西，

sentences.en: or is it something that we should somehow structurally address?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该以某种结构性方式解决的问题？

sentences.en: Spikes to stop people from sitting or lying down evoked a wide variety of reactions from the public.
sentences.zh: 阻止人们坐下或躺下的尖刺引起了公众的广泛反应。

sentences.en: The first time I saw someone lying here, a homeless couple actually,
sentences.zh: 我第一次看到有人躺在这里，实际上是一对无家可归的夫妇，

sentences.en: I didn't like it because I didn't like having to walk by them.
sentences.zh: 我并不喜欢它，因为我讨厌从他们身边走过。

sentences.en: That sounds very selfish.
sentences.zh: 这听起来很自私。

sentences.en: So when I saw those stats, I thought, good idea.
sentences.zh: 所以当我看到那些统计数据时，我想，这主意不错。

sentences.en: So a lot of people are bothered by the presence of homeless people,
sentences.zh: 因此，很多人对无家可归者的存在感到困扰，

sentences.en: but some are also alarmed by just how aggressive the spikes are.
sentences.zh: 但也有一些人对尖刺的攻击性感到震惊。

sentences.en: It almost looks harmful.
sentences.zh: 它看起来几乎有害。

sentences.en: You know, if you lie on those, you're going to get spiked.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你躺在上面，你会被扎到的。

sentences.en: And so it sends that message, which I think is wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以它传递了那样一个信息，我认为这是不对的。

sentences.en: It's worth saying that these spikes are not just in England.
sentences.zh: 值得一提的是，这些尖刺不仅在英国存在。

sentences.en: We have them in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 我们在美国

sentences.en: too.
sentences.zh: 也有。

sentences.en: Outside of our office is a window ledge where you naturally want to sit.
sentences.zh: 我们办公室外面有一个窗台，你自然会想坐在上面。

sentences.en: And sure enough, there are these black metal doorknob looking things that keep anyone from resting there.
sentences.zh: 果然，那里有一些黑色的金属门把手样式的物件，阻止任何人坐在那里休息。

sentences.en: And one thing that makes these spikes and similar features especially frustrating
sentences.zh: 让这些尖刺和类似设施尤其令人沮丧的一点是，

sentences.en: is that they're just there.
sentences.zh: 它们就杵在那里。

sentences.en: They're not moving.
sentences.zh: 它们不会动。

sentences.en: There's no arguing with them.
sentences.zh: 你无法与它们争辩。

sentences.en: You know, if you have a policeman who prohibits people from sleeping in a park,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你有一个警察禁止人们在公园里睡觉，

sentences.en: I think there is still some possible negotiation.
sentences.zh: 我认为仍然存在某种谈判的可能。

sentences.en: And I think that's good.
sentences.zh: 我认为这很好。

sentences.en: That's what society is about.
sentences.zh: 这正是社会的意义所在。

sentences.en: The ongoing negotiation and ongoing change.
sentences.zh: 持续的谈判和持续的改变。

sentences.en: But when we start using things that are immutable and unchangeable, like metal spikes,
sentences.zh: 但当我们开始使用那些固定不变、无法改变的东西时，比如金属尖刺，

sentences.en: there is nothing that is going to change until they ruSt.
sentences.zh: 在它们生锈之前，没有任何东西会改变。

sentences.en: I think that's the most important criteria for calling something unpleasant design.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是将某物称为不愉快设计的最重要标准。

sentences.en: It is something that you cannot negotiate with.
sentences.zh: 它是你无法与之谈判的东西。

sentences.en: We have all tried and probably failed to negotiate with one of the most common and aggravating forms
sentences.zh: 我们都曾试图并且可能未能与最常见、最令人恼火的形式进行谈判，

sentences.en: of unpleasant design, public seating.
sentences.zh: 那就是不愉快设计——公共座椅。

sentences.en: Whether it's in a park or at a bus stop or in an airport,
sentences.zh: 无论是在公园、公交车站还是在机场，

sentences.en: there are countless ways designers have made it so you cannot get comfortable
sentences.zh: 设计师们有无数种方法让你无法感到舒适，

sentences.en: and most especially cannot lie down.
sentences.zh: 尤其是绝对不能躺下。

sentences.en: A classic is the bench with armrests in between,
sentences.zh: 经典之作是带有中间扶手的长椅，

sentences.en: which of course let you rest your arm on the armreSt.
sentences.zh: 它当然能让你把胳膊放在扶手上。

sentences.en: But at the same time, they restrict any other kind of use than sitting upright.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，它们限制了除直立坐着以外的任何其他用途。

sentences.en: The only way this bench can be used is by three people sitting next to each other
sentences.zh: 这张长椅的唯一用法就是三个人并排坐着，

sentences.en: and not looking at each other, which is not the only thing you can do on a bench.
sentences.zh: 而且互不看对方，但这并不是你在长椅上唯一能做的事。

sentences.en: Especially it's not the only normal and legal thing you can do on a bench.
sentences.zh: 特别是，这并不是你在长椅上唯一能做的正常且合法的事。

sentences.en: Solana thinks that limiting the way something can be used is problematic.
sentences.zh: 索拉娜认为限制某物的用途是有问题的。

sentences.en: By attacking or addressing one particular problem,
sentences.zh: 通过攻击或解决一个特定的问题，

sentences.en: you actually generate many more problems and reduce complexity of possible behaviors in public space.
sentences.zh: 你实际上会产生更多的问题，并减少公共空间中可能行为的复杂性。

sentences.en: It's not just dividers and armrests.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是隔板和扶手的问题。

sentences.en: In the unpleasant design book, they also point out benches that are mounted so high
sentences.zh: 在《不愉快设计》一书中，他们还指出了一些安装得非常高的长椅，

sentences.en: that your feet can't touch the ground and therefore they're uncomfortable after a short period of time.
sentences.zh: 以至于你的脚无法触地，因此短时间内就会让人感到不舒服。

sentences.en: And they document an increased prevalence of leaning supports at bus stops
sentences.zh: 他们记录了公交车站上越来越多的靠扶，

sentences.en: that you can rest against while standing, but they do not accommodate sitting or sleeping.
sentences.zh: 你可以在站着的时候靠在上面休息，但它们不适合坐着或睡觉。

sentences.en: But the object that Solana considers the masterpiece of unpleasant design is the Camden Bench.
sentences.zh: 但索拉娜认为是不愉快设计巅峰之作的物体是卡姆登长椅。

sentences.en: Basically, it is a design solution to 22, I think, antisocial behavior probleMs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它是针对我认为有22个反社会行为问题提出的设计解决方案。

sentences.en: The only thing it does not deter is sitting.
sentences.zh: 它唯一无法阻止的就是坐着。

sentences.en: The Camden Bench, so named because it was commissioned by Camden London Borough Council,
sentences.zh: 卡姆登长椅因受伦敦卡姆登区议会委托而得名，

sentences.en: is a strange, angular, sculpted, solid lump of concrete with rounded edges and slopes in unexpected places.
sentences.zh: 它是一个奇怪的、有棱角的、雕塑般的、坚固的混凝土块，边缘圆润，在出人意料的地方有斜坡。

sentences.en: A critic on Medium named Frank Swain called it the perfect anti-object.
sentences.zh: Medium网站上一位名叫弗兰克·斯温的评论家称之为完美的抗对象。

sentences.en: Anti-sleeping because the shape makes it uncomfortable to sleep on.
sentences.zh: 防睡眠，因为这种形状让人睡在上面很不舒服。

sentences.en: Anti-drug dealing because there are no slots or crevices in which to hide drugs.
sentences.zh: 防毒品交易，因为没有可以藏毒的狭缝或缝隙。

sentences.en: Anti-theft because the recesses near the ground allow people to store bags behind their legs and away from would-be criminals.
sentences.zh: 防盗，因为靠近地面的凹槽允许人们将包藏在腿后，远离潜在的罪犯。

sentences.en: Anti-skateboard because the edges on the bench fluctuate in height, making grinding difficult.
sentences.zh: 防滑板，因为长椅上的边缘高度起伏不定，使得做招式变得困难。

sentences.en: Anti-litter because there are no surfaces or crevices where litter can accrue.
sentences.zh: 防垃圾，因为没有垃圾可以堆积的表面或缝隙。

sentences.en: Anti-graffiti because it has a special coating to repel paint.
sentences.zh: 防涂鸦，因为它有一层特殊的涂层来排斥油漆。

sentences.en: And all those goals are pretty noble.
sentences.zh: 所有这些目标都相当崇高。

sentences.en: Except for sleeping and skateboarding,
sentences.zh: 除了睡觉和玩滑板，

sentences.en: I don't really want the other activities happening in public spaces I go to either.
sentences.zh: 我其实也不希望其他活动发生在我去的公共空间里。

sentences.en: But Solonisavich finds this litany of anti-measures demoralizing.
sentences.zh: 但索拉娜·萨维奇觉得这一连串的防范措施令人沮丧。

sentences.en: It discourages 22 things.
sentences.zh: 它阻止了22件事。

sentences.en: It encourages two sitting and sitting together.
sentences.zh: 它只鼓励了两件事：坐着和坐在一起。

sentences.en: When we expect people to do bad things to the bench,
sentences.zh: 当我们预期人们会对长椅做坏事时，

sentences.en: before we think of anything good that people might do to this bench,
sentences.zh: 在我们想到人们可能对这把长椅做任何好事之前，

sentences.en: I think that's a very sad approach to public space.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一种对待公共空间非常悲哀的方式。

sentences.en: It's also a contagious approach to public space.
sentences.zh: 这也是一种具有传染性的对待公共空间的方式。

sentences.en: There's a chapter in the Unpleasant Design book that's devoted to all the unpleasant designs used to thwart pigeons in cities.
sentences.zh: 《不愉快设计》一书中有一章专门介绍城市中用来对付鸽子的各种不愉快设计。

sentences.en: Anti-pigeon spikes in nets are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 防鸽尖刺和网随处可见。

sentences.en: And even if you're like Solonisavich and aware of these measures and skeptical of our war on pigeons,
sentences.zh: 即使你像索拉娜·萨维奇一样了解这些措施并对我们的“鸽子战争”持怀疑态度，

sentences.en: you might not have a choice in whether or not to use them.
sentences.zh: 你可能也别无选择，只能使用它们。

sentences.en: A week after we have published the book, we had a confirmation of this.
sentences.zh: 在我们出版这本书的一周后，我们得到了一个印证。

sentences.en: We didn't even notice, but on the balcony doors, we actually had anti-pigeon spikes.
sentences.zh: 我们甚至没有注意到，但在阳台门上，我们实际上装有防鸽尖刺。

sentences.en: And then due to somebody hanging out on the balcony who was, I don't know, a bit clumsy,
sentences.zh: 然后由于某个人在阳台上闲逛，不知道怎么回事，有点笨手笨脚，

sentences.en: and they destroyed these spikes on one side, and we didn't even notice that,
sentences.zh: 他们把一侧的这些尖刺给毁坏了，而我们甚至都没有注意到这一点，

sentences.en: suddenly the balcony was filled with pigeon shit.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，阳台上堆满了鸽子屎。

sentences.en: Pigeons might not be overwhelming if the population is spread throughout a city,
sentences.zh: 如果鸽子数量分散在整个城市，可能还不会觉得太多，

sentences.en: but the ubiquity of pigeon spikes concentrate pigeons in the few places where there are no spikes.
sentences.zh: 但防鸽刺的无处不在，把鸽子集中到了仅有的几处没有防鸽刺的地方。

sentences.en: Solonis argues that's when the problem is created.
sentences.zh: 索洛尼斯认为，问题就是这样产生的。

sentences.en: And that should not be the way to solve any kind of interest conflicts over a space.
sentences.zh: 而这本不该是解决某种空间利益冲突的方式。

sentences.en: But yes, we immediately fixed our spikes.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，我们马上就把防鸽刺修理好了。

sentences.en: There is always an aspect of coercion to design.
sentences.zh: 设计中总会带有某种强制的成分。

sentences.en: Design is used to get you to buy things, to use your iPhone in a certain way,
sentences.zh: 设计被用来诱导你买东西、以某种特定方式使用你的 iPhone，

sentences.en: sometimes without you even being aware of it.
sentences.zh: 有时甚至在你毫无察觉的情况下。

sentences.en: And these pieces of hostile and unpleasant architecture are no different.
sentences.zh: 这些充满敌意且令人不悦的建筑设计也没有什么不同。

sentences.en: Design is something that is supposed to transmit a certain use of this object.
sentences.zh: 设计原本应该传达对这个物体的某种特定用法。

sentences.en: Otherwise, it would have not been designed.
sentences.zh: 否则，它就不会被设计出来了。

sentences.en: However, I think it is very problematic when we start excluding people by design.
sentences.zh: 然而，我认为当我们开始通过设计将人排挤在外时，这就成了很大的问题。

sentences.en: The reason we need a critical theory of unpleasant design
sentences.zh: 我们需要针对不悦设计建立批判性理论的原因，

sentences.en: is so we can recognize the coercion that is taking place in our public spaces.
sentences.zh: 是为了让我们能够认出公共空间中正在发生的强制行为。

sentences.en: We need to know when we're replacing human interaction and nuance and empathy
sentences.zh: 我们需要知道，当我们用生硬、物理且不容商榷的解决方案

sentences.en: with hard, physical, non-negotiable solutions.
sentences.zh: 去取代人与人之间的互动、细腻的情感与同理心时，到底意味着什么。

sentences.en: And this is what we wanted to achieve with this book, to start the debate.
sentences.zh: 这也是我们想通过这本书实现的目标，即开启这场辩论。

sentences.en: There will always be people who believe this is a good way and people who think it's terrible.
sentences.zh: 总会有人认为这是一种好方法，也有人觉得这糟透了。

sentences.en: And we are somehow not extreme in our opinion.
sentences.zh: 而我们的观点不知为何并不极端。

sentences.en: We're really the observers.
sentences.zh: 我们其实只是观察者。

sentences.en: And now you're an observer too.
sentences.zh: 现在你也是个观察者了。

sentences.en: Whether you think a certain form of design is exclusionary but serves a greater good,
sentences.zh: 无论你认为某种设计具有排他性但服务于更大的利益，

sentences.en: or just hostile and offensive,
sentences.zh: 还是仅仅觉得它充满敌意且冒犯，

sentences.en: it's important to be aware of the decisions that are being made for you.
sentences.zh: 意识到那些为你做出的决定是很重要的。

sentences.en: Because most likely, unpleasant design is put there to make things more pleasant
sentences.zh: 因为很有可能，不悦设计的存在是为了让某些人觉得更愉快，

sentences.en: for someone just like you.
sentences.zh: 而那些人就像你一样。
